clue.text: Aggressive guy taking dope to sicken a social worker

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass
to ail is to be sick or make sick
the ant is a social insect and a worker in its colony

explanation.surface: A thug drugs himself in order to harm a welfare officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a welfare officer; in crosswords it is usually the ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An attacker is someone who assails, a person who behaves aggressively towards a victim.

clue.text: Wrestle in order to perspire copiously

indicators.note: putting the letters of the word into a new order signals rearrangement

explanation.surface: A wrestler works up a heavy sweat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' rearranges WRESTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To swelter is to suffer from great heat, sweating heavily.

clue.text: Hoped for some publicity about a section of the church

indicators.note: the publicity word goes round the other pieces, surrounding them

parts.note: an ad is a piece of publicity
a spire is part of a church building

explanation.surface: Someone wishing for some press coverage of a church department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some publicity' is a short form of advertisement; 'about' signals the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire to something is to aim or long for it, a synonym of hoped for.

clue.text: Drink-all the GI wanted

indicators.note: taken as 'lacking order', the letters of the following words are wanted in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Every American soldier was after a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanted' signals the anagram of ALL THE GI; it is a loose indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Light ale is a pale beer, a kind of drink.

clue.text: The gift of a story book

parts.note: a tale is a story
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A storybook given as a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' is the crossword convention NT, the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural aptitude, often called a gift.

clue.text: Faded-without charm-so broken up

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, the faded word stands round the charm word

parts.note: something that faded away died
a spell is a magic charm

explanation.surface: Something faded once its charm wore off and was broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Clouds or crowds that are dispelled are driven away and scattered.

clue.text: Person providing food for a pet with much hesitation

parts.note: a cat is a pet

indicators.note: a lot of hesitating means the sound is given more than once, here twice

parts.note: er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Feeding an animal while dithering a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much' doubles ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer supplies meals, for example at functions.

clue.text: It helps to protect the frog, lucky thing?

definitions.text: It helps to protect the frog
definitions.meaning: the frog is the soft pad on the underside of a horse's hoof, shielded by a curved iron
the curved iron hung over a door is a traditional good-luck charm

explanation.definitionFit: The iron fixed to a hoof guards its frog, and the same object is a familiar emblem of good fortune.

clue.text: A fighter, thanks to stirring music

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
ta is informal British for thanks
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier shows gratitude for rousing tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitato is a musical direction for an agitated, restless style of playing.

clue.text: Interview a young attendant and discharge

parts.note: to see someone can mean to interview them
a page is a boy attendant

explanation.surface: Meet a pageboy and then dismiss him.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is liquid slowly leaking out, a discharge.

clue.text: Fast organised by former newspapermen

parts.note: ex means former
the press are journalists collectively

explanation.surface: A hunger strike arranged by ex-journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like a noun for not eating; it means quick.
explanation.definitionFit: An express train or delivery is a fast one.

clue.text: Repeating it, point to budget

parts.note: taken as written
E is a compass point, east
a ration is a fixed allowance, a budget

explanation.surface: Saying it again, an adviser points to the budget.
explanation.walkthrough: E for east is the usual crossword 'point'.
explanation.definitionFit: Iteration is the act of doing or saying something again, repetition.

clue.text: Some sporting people who never see the way ahead

definitions.text: Some sporting people who never see the way ahead

parts.words: Some sporting people who never see the way ahead
parts.note: rowers sit facing the stern, so they move backwards and cannot see where they are going

explanation.definitionFit: Rowers sit with their backs to the direction of travel, so they never face forward.

clue.text: Tiles are made in such workshops

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Tiles get produced in places like these.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges TILES ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's studio, a workshop.

clue.text: Charge a pound-about right for a wedding?

indicators.note: the charge, a and pound words go round the right word

parts.note: to bid someone do something is to charge or command them
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Charging a pound or so seems right for a marriage service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts BIDAL round R, which sits after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridal describes anything belonging to a bride or her marriage ceremony.

clue.text: Lawyer, a really good man, entrapped by a fence

indicators.note: the saint is caught inside the fence word

parts.note: a barrier is a fence
ST stands for saint, a very good person

explanation.surface: A lawyer, a saintly fellow, is caught behind a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: ST, short for saint, is the usual crossword 'good man'; 'entrapped by' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister is a lawyer who argues cases in the higher courts.

clue.text: They agree a ship lists

parts.note: SS is steamship
to enter items is to list or record them

explanation.surface: People say yes when a vessel heels over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lists' looks like a ship leaning; it means records.
explanation.definitionFit: Assenters are people who assent, giving agreement.

clue.text: Disease may be spread by water

indicators.note: spreading the letters around shuffles them into a new order

explanation.surface: Illness can be transmitted through water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be spread' rearranges DISEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: The seaside is the coast, land beside the sea.

clue.text: A Northerner not used to high living

definitions.text: A Northerner not used to high living

parts.words: A Northerner not used to high living
parts.note: a person from northern England who lives in a valley, so not living high up rather than not living lavishly

explanation.definitionFit: A dalesman lives in the valleys of northern England, such as Yorkshire, low ground rather than hilltops.

clue.text: … into the middle of a burning fiery "(OT Daniel)

definitions.text: into the middle of a burning fiery

parts.words: into the middle of a burning fiery
parts.note: the Book of Daniel tells of three men cast into the midst of a burning fiery oven-like chamber; the missing last word completes the quotation

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from Daniel 3 in the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament phrase about Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego ends with the great kiln that Nebuchadnezzar heated.

clue.text: These days a bog engenders respect

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era
a mire is a bog

explanation.surface: A modern swamp inspires esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: AD (anno Domini) is the current era, hence 'these days'.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to look up to and esteem them.

clue.text: Erasmus could be such a manipulator

indicators.note: the letters of the name could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: The scholar Erasmus might have been a manipulative schemer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges ERASMUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur manipulates muscles as a profession.

clue.text: Bill's settled, as this makes plain

definitions.text: Bill's settled, as this makes plain

parts.words: Bill's settled, as this makes plain
parts.note: the slip given after payment shows that an account has been paid

explanation.definitionFit: A receipt is the written acknowledgement that money has been paid.

clue.text: Game profligate cut by a fellow from the Baltic

indicators.note: the profligate word is split open by the Baltic word

parts.note: a roue is a dissolute rake, a profligate
a Lett is a Latvian

explanation.surface: A rake is wounded by a Latvian over a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lett is a native of Latvia on the Baltic; 'cut by' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino gambling game played with a spinning wheel.

clue.text: Abuse one may get in traffic

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the traffic word

parts.note: trade and traffic both mean dealing in goods
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The road rage a driver may suffer in heavy traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' looks like cars on roads; it means trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech, a stream of verbal abuse.

clue.text: Awful cretin set to cause split

indicators.note: the letters are in an awful state and must be reordered

explanation.surface: A dreadful fool is set to divide people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges CRETIN SET.
explanation.definitionFit: To intersect is to cut across, dividing something into parts.

clue.text: Some have chosen a Tory politician

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are taken, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A few people have picked a Conservative as their politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals the run spanning the end of 'chosen', the 'a' and the start of 'Tory'.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, an elected politician.

clue.text: Nobody can recall being affected by this

definitions.text: Nobody can recall being affected by this

parts.words: Nobody can recall being affected by this
parts.note: a condition that wipes out memory, so sufferers cannot remember having had it

explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, so a sufferer may not remember the illness itself.

clue.text: Aim to retain the inner part-it will be wanted again

indicators.note: the aim word holds the inner part inside it

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose
the core is the inner part

explanation.surface: Aiming to keep the essence, a performer is called back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retain' signals the container; the definition is in the past tense, as in 'the song was wanted again'.
explanation.definitionFit: A performance that was encored was called for again by the audience.

clue.text: Clear one troublesome pest found in the river

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the river word

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a crossword favourite
taken as written
a rat is a pest

explanation.surface: Clearing a rodent pest out of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to clear someone of blame.
